extracted.intended_audience: government contracting officers, DoD program managers, and defense contractors involved in Value Engineering (VE) and VECPs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and practical standards for implementing Value Engineering (VE) and processing Value Engineering Change Proposals (VECPs) under the new OMB Circular A-131 within federal acquisition. Covers contract clauses, incentives, application to services, interactions with LEAN/Six Sigma, and suggested FAR revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: VECP must lead to a change in the contract (FAR 52.248-1(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: VE FAR 52.248-1(b)(1) mandates that a VECP must lead to a change in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some contracting officers interpret this to mean the VECP must change the specification or at least the Statement of Work; others accept a VECP as a 'change in the contract' even if it is implemented without a formal spec change. The new Circular A-131 sanctions accepting VECPs as changes in some cases, reducing prior uncertainty about what constitutes a 'contract change.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared savings calculation and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Shared savings are computed from gross VECP savings less contractor development & implementation costs and government costs, producing Net Acquisition Savings (NAS) which is then split between contractor (KR) and government according to the share rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (Figure 1) shows calculation: Instant Unit Cost Reduction × number of units = Gross VECP; subtract CADIC and government costs = NAS; apply share rates (e.g., 50/50) to determine contractor and government shares. Contracting officers should have flexibility to negotiate more equitable sharing rates when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor incentive / profit treatment for VECPs
rubrics_metrics.description: VECPs can increase contractor profit by allowing the contractor to receive a share of realized savings in addition to original contract profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates original profit plus contractor share of VE savings yields a higher new profit. This incentive helps overcome contractor reluctance to propose savings that would otherwise reduce their revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative instant contract savings handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When nonrecurring costs of a change exceed instant (current contract) savings (negative instant contract savings), the VECP clause allows adding that negative amount to the contract price and offsetting it against the contractor's share of future savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treatment enables LEAN, Six Sigma, or other projects with upfront costs but longer-term savings to be proposed as VECPs and recoup development costs via future contract savings shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply VE to services (address measurement and baseline issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular A-131 renews emphasis on expanding VE into services, recognizing current clause language focuses on 'per unit' savings that fit hardware better than services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services pose challenges: per-hour pricing could rise after hours reduction due to amortized costs; IDIQ contracts lack firm baselines for demonstrating savings. The recommended approach is to require VECPs for services to propose how savings should be measured, how development costs will be paid, and how shared savings will be verified and paid (see recommended FAR subparagraph). Existing payment mechanisms might be adaptable but official precedents and clause language changes are likely needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require VECP submissions for services to propose measurement, payment, and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: "On a VECP for services, propose how savings should be measured, development costs paid, and shared savings verified and paid."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends adding a subparagraph to FAR 52.248-1 obligating contractors to address these points in their VECP submittal, placing the onus on the contractor and giving contracting officers maximum flexibility to accept VECPs for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow LEAN and Six Sigma projects to be processed as VECPs
rubrics_metrics.description: The new Circular A-131 states LEAN and Six Sigma can go hand in hand with VE, placing those projects on equal footing with VE for potential VECP processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some LEAN/Six Sigma projects are not contract-specific or would not require a contract change, the Circular's recognition enables them to be proposed as VECPs; this helps address earlier rejections due to inability to share future savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify FAR clause 52.248-1 to simplify and increase flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR 52.248-1 has remained largely unchanged and contains provisions (e.g., proscription against reductions in items to be delivered) that may prevent beneficial VECPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article suggests simplifying the clause and giving contracting officers flexibility (including negotiating share rates and accepting changes previously proscribed) so the government can benefit from proposals that might otherwise be excluded by rigid clause language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address VE on services via new clause or FAR subparagraph if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: A new clause specifically addressing VECPs for services (analogous to FAR 52.248-3 for construction) may be the long-term solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a short-term fix could be modifying the basic clause with a subparagraph addressing VECP submittal requirements for services (measurement, payment, verification) and granting contracting officers flexibility; experience from such submissions would inform a separate services clause later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mandatory VE studies on major program starts to jump-start VE in services
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to 1988 DoD required Mandatory VE programs on major program starts where the government funded separate line items requiring contractors to perform VE studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends considering a Mandatory VE clause on service contracts over $100M and having program offices withhold a small budget percentage (e.g., 0.5%) to fund mandatory VE studies. Contracts could then require the VECP to address measurement and payment/share arrangements. Government-funded studies typically reduce the contractor's share of savings but seed VE activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a life-cycle savings fund at PEO level
rubrics_metrics.description: Life-cycle savings (operating and support) are often realized over many years and are hard to fund/reward under current mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal: create a fund at the Program Executive Office (PEO) level resourced by taking a percentage of hardware acquisition money, replenished as savings are achieved, to cover development costs and savings sharing for life-cycle VECPs across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collateral savings sharing (life-cycle / non-acquisition savings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAR allows contractors to receive 20–100% of a typical year's collateral savings as reward for a VECP that yields non-acquisition savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is uncertainty because the contracting officer determines the 'typical year's savings' at sole discretion; this discretion can create unpredictability for contractors considering such VECPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutionalize VE in program reviews and require VE training
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful contractors require VE to be addressed in each internal program review (e.g., a chart showing VECPs submitted, planned, and under consideration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government program managers could require similar inclusion of VE in program reviews to institutionalize VE. Additionally, both government and contractor personnel should take VE training developed by the Federal Procurement Institute and the Defense Acquisition University as part of Circular A-131 implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow program managers to retain and use a portion of VE savings/incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Program managers should be allowed to retain a substantial part of VE savings or incentives received from successful VECPs and use those savings on the program as they see fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This retention aligns incentives: program managers who assume risk for VE changes would have tangible rewards, encouraging them to pursue VE. Incorporating this in a circular is difficult, but contractors and some organizations have implemented such practices as best practices to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and address barriers that discourage contractor VECP submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Barriers include contractors' reluctance to propose changes that lower their revenues, additional processing burden/time to process VECPs, lack of experience/training in processing VECPs, fear of criticism for giving contractors a windfall, and difficulties estimating future savings and sharing operating/support costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circular A-131 addresses many issues and encourages VE; solutions proposed include clearer clause language, share-rate flexibility, funding mechanisms for life-cycle savings, training, and program-level incentives to reduce these barriers.
